notes:
Context: Silkbridge builds an IDE-integrated developer productivity suite used internally and sold to large enterprises. Their product requires near-instant streaming completions inside editor panes and a nightly/higher-frequency embedding refresh pipeline for code search/indexing.

Key constraints and asks:
- Streaming: sub-30ms median token delivery, 95th <80ms inside IDE (PST developer locations). Must support token-by-token streaming over unreliable mobile networks.
- Determinism: ability to pin model+weights for reproducible suggestions across releases; explicit rollback and A/B canary controls.
- Background throughput: embedding refresh must handle bursts of 4-6M files during weekly monorepo syncs; target steady-state embedding throughput 80k-120k embeddings/min during refresh windows. They plan incremental delta detection and want Redwood to recommend batch sizes and retry semantics.
- Cost profile: prefer using quantized open models for background embedding jobs; want policies to route interactive completions to a high-SLA Dedicated pool while batching/quoting background jobs to cheaper capacity.
- Ops/Security: require VPC peering + option for on-prem private control plane for EU customers; needs KMS integration and per-request audit logging; retention controls for telemetry and suggestion logs.

POC plan summary:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Hosted demo for streaming UX and model pinning demo + small-scale embedding refresh (100k files)
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Dedicated perf run (3-node GPU pool) for tail-latency and streaming token jitter measurements; run synthetic embedding bulk load to validate throughput vs cost settings
- Phase 3: Procurement for 6-month reserved capacity or hybrid (Dedicated + Private for EU customers)

SE notes / action items:
- Provide warmup script and recommended prefix/KV cache priming steps (Aisha)
- Share embedding batching guidelines (suggested initial batch ~2048, max 4096 for quantized models) and retry idempotency patterns
- Draft VPC peering runbook and expected firewall rules for their SREs by 2026-03-18
